messages.text: Without commentary, introduction, summary, quotation marks, pull out all of the most interesting, intriguing, and surprising standalone sentences.

Winning is achieved by either providing a correct translation or uncovering a fraud
1
.
Some cards are printed with fluorescing ink that reveals a new layer of the game under a black light
2
.
The Ladies of the Order is a fictional group with no documented historical connection to the manuscript
3
.
The Internet Conspiracy Theorist uses a special ability to corrupt data and trigger a collapse of consensus
4

.
Athanasius Kircher wins the game specifically when confusion triumphs over clarity
6
.
Magic Eye easter eggs are hidden within the designs on the backs of the cards
7
.
Sir Francis Bacon is the creator of an evil-looking tincture
8
.
If the manuscript is proven to be gibberish, players must verify the perpetrator of the fraud to win
9

.
The game features a total of 8,114 different Word cards, though only a subset is included in the base set

.
Players are seated in chronological order based on their character’s era, with those to the left representing the past and those to the right representing the future
11

.
The Amphora card allows players to seal secrets face down in a cache to keep them safe from prying eyes
13
.
A player who draws an Author Card must secretly decide whether to conceal their identity through their future voting patterns
14

.
Grapholalia allows a player to gain influence even when their translation proposals are voted down by the group
16

.
A mysterious Aztec priestess acts as the keeper of a flying salve
18
19
.
Players establish character lifespans by rolling percentile dice to determine an age at death between 18 and 100
